title: Bones together or apart?
hook: A fossil can preserve different kinds of arrangement.

knows: A skeleton is made of bones connected at joints.
doesNotKnow: Identify what an articulated fossil preserves about relative position.

misconception: The same list of bones always preserves the same information about their arrangement.
objective: Identify what an articulated fossil preserves about relative position.

claims.text: A fossil can preserve different kinds of arrangement. Two schematic fossils preserve the same bones. In which are the bones still arranged together as they were in the body? The connected specimen preserves bones together at their joints; the other shows separated bones. Articulation can provide positional evidence, but this drawing alone does not establish the cause or timing of separation.
claims.source: Source lead for independent checking: Smithsonian https://naturalhistory.si.edu/collections/paleobiology. The skeletal diagrams are schematic and not specimens.

claims.text: The schematic figure and its chosen timing, species or measurements represent the explicitly stated example and are not photographic evidence of an individual specimen.

claims.text: Recall: Two fossil bones remain connected at a joint. What extra evidence does the connection supply? A connection at a joint provides positional information.
